title: Real-time Experiments with an AI Co-Scientist - Stefania Druga, fmr. Google Deepmind
talk_summary: A demo-heavy talk about a real-time 'AI co-scientist' that fuses live sensor, camera, and voice inputs into a dynamically assembled context sent to Gemini, plus a recap of DeepMind's multi-agent co-scientist paper. The transferable engineering idea is a modality-aware context assembler that rebuilds the prompt each turn from whatever inputs are currently connected.

takeaways.what_they_do: A 'context assembly' layer inspects which input modalities are present (text, voice, image, chat history, sensor streams) on every message and builds the prompt from only those, rather than a fixed template.

takeaways.technique: Role-specialized agents with a ranking/aggregation step
takeaways.what_they_do: Describes DeepMind's co-scientist as separate agents doing literature search, summarization, hypothesis generation, and ranking, then aggregating ranked outputs into a plan for the human.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they actually created uh an orchestration of different agents. Each of them was actually working on Gemini... with this orchestration of like ranking the different results

takeaways.what_they_do: The co-scientist was validated by replaying a discovery that originally took 12 years and checking whether the system could reproduce it without having seen the data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they actually tested it against prior discoveries... a discovery that took scientists 12 years. Uh it took the AI scientist two days

takeaways.technique: Uniform webhook ingestion for heterogeneous inputs
takeaways.what_they_do: All input sources (USB sensors, webcams, text, voice) are normalized into webhooks consumed by one backend, so adding a sensor doesn't change the pipeline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all of these like inputs become web hooks and I can... that gets sent to a back end which communicates with the real API

takeaways.technique: Cheap commodity hardware for the harness
takeaways.what_they_do: Whole real-time rig built from off-the-shelf open-source parts for under $300 in two weeks, deliberately scoped to what could run and be measured live.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the cost of all the parts uh is under $300 and it took me two weeks to build it and it's open source
